config.victim_selection: the first attempt's script: query jobs WHERE status='running' for lease owners (docker compose exec api python, several seconds under CPU throttling), SIGKILL that worker, then query again for running jobs leased to it

what_happened: Both SIGKILLs hit worker d82239faee54 (qbt-worker-2) after the job it had been running finished: the query after the kill found no running job leased to it. A job still leased to a dead worker stays 'running' until its 30 s lease expires, so that query would have seen one; no job was interrupted by either kill.

Before the third kill attempt the script rescaled to 2 workers with `--wait`. The other worker, qbt-worker-1 (never killed), had its healthcheck (a Python start-up inside the container, 5 s timeout) time out at the CPU-credit baseline, so Compose reported it unhealthy and the command failed. aws_bench.py raised and exited.

The diagnosis a minute later: both workers running, healthy again, restarts=0; health log shows two 'Health check exceeded timeout (5s)' followed by passes; worker logs show jobs claimed at attempt 1 and succeeding (3.4-3.8 s at the baseline). Memory 1,056 of 1,909 MiB used, load average 2.27.
The process exiting stopped the Poisson submission part-way; the 40-job backlog had been submitted. The workers kept processing what was queued.

integrity.why: The run aborted before its checks. The third attempt began with reset() (DELETE FROM jobs) at 21:33:34Z, which removed the second attempt's jobs, including any still queued or running, so lost/duplicated/stuck/completed-twice can't be determined after the fact; the database no longer exists.
integrity.evidence_available: Neither kill interrupted a job, so requeue and fencing were never exercised in this attempt. Every worker log line in the diagnosis is attempt 1 and 'succeeded'; none shows 'result discarded' or a lease error. That is 12 jobs, not all of them.
integrity.effect_on_attempt_3: Attempt 3's checks count only jobs submitted after its own reset and read worker logs only from after it; it found 0 extra jobs, 0 fencing rejections and 0 discarded results, so nothing from attempt 2 showed up in it.

fixes_before_attempt_3: kill triggered by a worker's own 'claimed job' log line (no Python start-up between seeing the claim and the SIGKILL), then confirm the job is still running
scale() waits for the containers to be running, not healthy
